response.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT z.city, COUNT(DISTINCT a.link_to_member) AS cnt FROM attendance a JOIN member m ON m.member_id = a.link_to_member JOIN zip_code z ON z.zip_code = m.zip GROUP BY z.city), s AS (SELECT city, cnt, cnt * 1.0 / SUM(cnt) OVER () AS share FROM c), o AS (SELECT city, cnt, share, AVG(share) OVER () AS avg_share FROM s) SELECT AVG(cnt) AS avg_count, AVG(share) AS avg_share, AVG(share - avg_share) AS avg_excess_over_overall_avg FROM o WHERE share > avg_share

assumptions.assumption: Cities are grouped by city name alone, so zip codes in different states that share a city name are merged into one city.
The three averages are taken over only the above-average cities. The overall average share is the mean of share across all cities, which equals 1 divided by the number of cities.
Members with no zip, or whose zip is not in zip_code, are dropped by the inner joins. Since the shares are computed over the remaining members, they sum to 1.

alternatives.interpretation: A city is identified by city name plus state, so same-named cities in different states stay separate.
alternatives.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT z.city, z.state, COUNT(DISTINCT a.link_to_member) AS cnt FROM attendance a JOIN member m ON m.member_id = a.link_to_member JOIN zip_code z ON z.zip_code = m.zip GROUP BY z.city, z.state), s AS (SELECT city, state, cnt, cnt * 1.0 / SUM(cnt) OVER () AS share FROM c), o AS (SELECT city, state, cnt, share, AVG(share) OVER () AS avg_share FROM s) SELECT AVG(cnt) AS avg_count, AVG(share) AS avg_share, AVG(share - avg_share) AS avg_excess_over_overall_avg FROM o WHERE share > avg_share
